title: Migrate the opportunity_pipeline XML workflow to a Python transition function
target_requirement: Reimplement the opportunity_pipeline workflow as a Python module exposing fire(state, event, record) that returns {state, record, audits, notifies, matched}, preserving legacy engine semantics: guard evaluation with VRL coercions (empty string to 0, sentinel date equality), first-match-in-document-order transition selection, set actions applied after the state change in order, and the WF_NOMATCH no-op for unmatched events.
expected_behavior: fire() returns the new state with set/audit/notify actions of the fired transition applied in order; a guarded transition whose guard is FALSE does not fire; an event with no matching transition returns the same state, an unmodified record copy, audits ['WF_NOMATCH'], and matched False; the input record is never mutated.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §3) and workflows.xml.
security_expectations: No network access; the module must not import network or subprocess modules; notify actions are returned as data, never dispatched.
failure_conditions: Treating an unmatched event as an error instead of a WF_NOMATCH no-op; mutating the input record; applying set actions when the guard failed; skipping guard evaluation; nondeterminism.
